sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Founded by **Haji Shariatullah** in 1818 in Faridpur, Bengal. 
• **Ideology**: Advocated for **'Faraiz'** (obligatory duties of Islam), rejecting syncretic practices. 
• **Evolution**: Shifted from religious purification to **agrarian militancy** under Dudu Miyan. 
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement was strictly **anti-landlord** and **anti-planter**, focusing on the protection of the rights of the **raiyats** (tenants) against illegal cesses (abwabs).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Led by Haji Shariatullah; focused on Faridpur/Dacca; puritanical Islam.
Reaction to moral decay and influence of Hindu customs.
Led by Dudu Miyan; organized 'Lathials' (armed guards); parallel administration.
Resistance against high rents and indigo planter oppression.

items.definition: Son of Shariatullah; transformed the movement into a revolutionary organization by dividing Bengal into 'halkas' (circles) with appointed deputies.
Armed bands of peasants organized by Dudu Miyan to defend the Faraizis against the physical coercion of zamindars and indigo planters.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Parallel Governance**: Established a system of justice and tax collection independent of the British courts.
• **Social Solidarity**: Promoted the concept of 'Dar-ul-Islam' (land of Islam) vs 'Dar-ul-Harb' (land of war).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Severe repression by the British administration and the combined might of Hindu/Muslim landlords.
• **Solutions**: The movement eventually merged into the broader Wahabi movement, losing its distinct agrarian focus.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-A-R-A-I-Z-I' -> **F**aridpur, **A**grarian, **R**eform, **A**nti-planter, **I**slam, **Z**amindar, **I**ndigo.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Covers the location, nature, objective, and primary targets of the revolt.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Faraizi with the Wahabi movement. Remember: Faraizi was localized in Bengal and focused on agrarian rights, whereas Wahabi was a pan-Islamic revivalist movement with a broader geographical scope.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Resistance' to describe the Faraizi movement, highlighting how religious identity provided the organizational structure for economic protest.

keyTakeaways: The Faraizi movement was a classic example of religious identity being used as a tool for peasant mobilization.
Dudu Miyan's organizational structure (halkas) was a precursor to modern political party mobilization.
The movement highlights the failure of the Permanent Settlement to protect the interests of the actual cultivators.
